comments.content: The absolute `/home/leviathan` user-home path is hardcoded. This makes the module non-portable: any move of the home directory or reuse on another host breaks the path resolution silently. If this must be environment-specific, at least document the assumption clearly, or prefer resolving from an environment variable / `os.homedir()` at runtime. (UI-text relaxation does not apply here — these are filesystem business paths.)

comments.content: The `norm` constant is computed but never used in the loop — the comparisons reference `absPath` directly instead of the normalized `norm`. As a result, the trailing-slash normalization (removing a trailing `/`) has no effect on the result, and paths with a trailing slash won't match `keep` exactly. Use `norm` in the comparison: `if (norm === keep || norm.startsWith(keep + "/")) return true;`.

The trailing-slash normalization is incomplete: it only strips one trailing slash via `slice(0, -1)`. A path like `/foo/bar//` becomes `/foo/bar/`, which still ends with `/` and therefore won't equal any `keep` value or `keep + "/"`. Consider normalizing with a regex (`.replace(//+$/, "")`) or `path.normalize()`. For robustness and cross-platform correctness, prefer importing Node's `path` utilities.
